case.pattern_description: Coordinated cross-card online fraud originating from a specific device profile (Samsung SM-G935F Build/NRD90M on Chrome Android) routing through an anonymous proxy. The perpetrator executes unauthorized online purchases across multiple unrelated card accounts without fitting documented typologies, matching the undocumented pattern previously confirmed on this device in CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035.
connected_device_profiles: SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080

evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3462447 was conducted online for $225.36 using device D004630, which was new to this account and masked behind an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS).

Device D004630 belongs to fraud ring 57672119 and was used within 48 hours to make online purchases on three other cards (C10326-K1, C13487-K1, and C08168-K1), appearing as a new device behind an anonymous proxy on each account.

Device D004630 is directly tied to four confirmed-fraud closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2985, CC-2971, CC-3035) where analysts confirmed unauthorized online purchases from this specific Samsung SM-G935F profile behind an anonymous proxy.

Holder C01996-K2|441|110 had only one prior transaction (tx 3382692 for $49.97, in-person, product W), making flagged online transaction 3462447 for $225.36 in product C an unprecedented channel and product departure.

The bank's second-generation fraud model gave transaction 3462447 a low score of 0.061 (historical fraud rate of 0.1138) and a legacy risk score of 0.33, indicating that intrinsic transaction features did not trigger standard alert thresholds.
The billing region on flagged transaction 3462447 is region 441, which matches the billing region of holder C01996-K2|441|110 and their prior in-person transaction 3382692.

evidence.claim: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

Rule R6: Shared origin: Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

case.summary: Monitoring flagged transaction 3462447 ($225.36) on card C01996-K2 after it was conducted online using device D004630, which was new to this account and masked behind an anonymous proxy. Graph analysis revealed that device D004630 belongs to fraud ring 57672119, made purchases across three other cards within 48 hours, and is directly linked to four confirmed-fraud closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2985, CC-2971, and CC-3035). Although the transaction occurred in the holder's billing region and received a low intrinsic model score of 0.061, the cross-card links and departure from the holder's single prior in-person transaction are highly suspicious. The case is assessed as uncertain with a 0.492 probability of undocumented fraud, and has been escalated to an analyst while connected cards are monitored.
